# Authority and file ownership

Every committed LORE surface has one owner and one mutation path. A generated file is never repaired by editing the projection itself.

| Surface | Classification | Direct editing | Owner or regeneration path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lore.yaml` | Authoritative configuration | Yes, with schema review | Repository maintainer |
| `schemas/` | Authoritative protocol contracts | Yes, with compatibility review | Schema implementation |
| `.lore/extracted/` | Deterministic generated facts | No | `lore extract` |
| `.lore/records/` | Accepted semantic history | No in-place edits | Validated `lore-proposal/v1` through `lore apply` |
| `.lore/proposals/` | Untrusted candidate input | Yes | Human or external maintainer |
| `.lore/transactions/` | Accepted transaction receipts | No | `lore apply` |
| `docs/generated/` | Deterministic documentation | No | `lore project` |
| `skills/` | Versioned maintainer protocol | Yes, with digest and compatibility review | Repository maintainer |
| Local caches and dependency stores | Runtime state | Local only | Package manager or operating environment |

## Safe change order

1. Change implementation, configuration, schemas, or other authoritative source.
2. Regenerate deterministic facts with `lore extract`.
3. Generate bounded maintainer context.
4. Validate and review one proposal.
5. Apply the accepted transaction.
6. Regenerate projections with `lore project`.
7. Verify the final tree and review the semantic diff.
